_README: TEMPLATE — copy this file to data/<set-id>/<set-id>-NN.json and fill it in.
Delete these two underscore keys when you're done; they are ignored by the site.
After adding a file you must also add an entry for it in data/index.json.
DIFFICULTY PROGRESSION:
Every worksheet's five questions get harder in a fixed order:
Q1-Q3: easy — answerable just by reading the paragraph once.
Q4:    hard — takes a bit of lateral thinking to work out.
Q5:    very hard — takes a lot of critical thinking to work out.
All five must still be answerable using ONLY the paragraph. Q4 and Q5 get
harder because they require connecting or reasoning about details in the
paragraph, not because they require outside knowledge.
HOW 'order' WORKS:
Each question stores the correct answer once ('correct') and three wrong answers
('distractors'). The 'order' array decides which of those four appears as A, B, C, D.
Token 'c'  = the correct answer.
Token 'd0' = distractors[0], 'd1' = distractors[1], 'd2' = distractors[2].
Because 'order' is saved in the file, the choices print in the SAME order every
time, so one answer key always works for every printed copy.
Example: "order": ["d1", "c", "d2", "d0"] prints as
A. distractors[1]   B. correct   C. distractors[2]   D. distractors[0]
...which makes the answer to that question B.
Vary the position of 'c' across the five questions so the key isn't all one letter.
'correctLetter' must match wherever you put 'c'. Run tools/validate.py to check.
_CHECKLIST: Every question is answerable from the paragraph alone — no outside knowledge.
Q1-Q3 are easy — a single read of the paragraph is enough to answer them.
Q4 is hard — it takes a bit of lateral thinking to work out.
Q5 is very hard — it takes a lot of critical thinking to work out.
Distractors are plausible but clearly wrong to a careful reader.
'c' is not in the same slot for all five questions.
'correctLetter' agrees with the position of 'c' in 'order'.
Paragraph is one self-contained block — no headings, lists, or line breaks.
title: Worksheet 1: Topic Name Here
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: Write one self-contained paragraph here, roughly 110 to 190 words. It should define the concept, then give a concrete example or short scenario. Every question below must be answerable using only this paragraph. Keep it as a single block of prose with no line breaks, headings, or bullet points, since the printable view renders it as one bordered box. Give the paragraph enough concrete detail (numbers, a stated rule, a worked example) that questions 4 and 5 have something specific to reason from.

questions.text: An easy question whose answer is stated plainly in the paragraph (Q1 — easy, single read):
questions.correct: The answer, stated the way the paragraph states it
distractors: A third plausible but incorrect option

questions.text: A second easy question, also answerable on a single read (Q2 — easy, single read):
A third easy question, also answerable on a single read (Q3 — easy, single read):

A hard question that takes a bit of lateral thinking — give a new situation and ask students to apply a rule or example from the paragraph to it (Q4 — hard, lateral thinking, still answerable from the paragraph alone):
questions.correct: The conclusion that follows from applying the paragraph's rule
distractors: A conclusion that misapplies the rule
A conclusion that reverses the rule
A conclusion the paragraph does not support

questions.text: A very hard question that takes a lot of critical thinking — ask students to weigh two details against each other, spot an implication, or explain why something happens, based on the paragraph (Q5 — very hard, critical thinking, still answerable from the paragraph alone):
questions.correct: The supported conclusion, with the reason included in the option text
distractors: A conclusion that ignores a stated condition
A conclusion that contradicts the paragraph
